title: Writing the General Solution
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: When an interval is not specified, trigonometric equations are often expressed using a general solution that represents every possible angle.

content.text: The symbol n is usually used to represent any integer, allowing the formula to generate infinitely many solutions.
The general solution depends on the period of the trigonometric function involved.

formulas.name: Sine General Solution
formulas.expression: sin(x) = a  ⇒  x = (−1)ⁿ sin⁻¹(a) + nπ, n ∈ ℤ

formulas.name: Tangent General Solution
formulas.expression: tan(x) = a  ⇒  x = tan⁻¹(a) + nπ, n ∈ ℤ

examples.question: Find the general solution of tan(x) = √3.
examples.solution: The reference angle is π/3. Since tangent repeats every π, x = π/3 + nπ, where n ∈ ℤ.

key_ideas: The period determines how solutions repeat.
misconceptions: Using 2π as the period for tangent.
Giving only solutions in one revolution when a general solution is required.
